title: Don't Cast His Warnings into the Fire
summary: The king cut up God's word and burned it. Are there warnings of God we are functionally burning? Pursue the Lord with your whole heart.
exhortation: The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, and he wrote it down on a scroll. It must have taken quite some time. His servant brought it before the king. And instead of responding in humility, piece by piece and with deliberateness, the king cut off the warnings of the Lord and threw them into the fire. What arrogance. When I read this, my stomach tightened at the thought of throwing the word of God, the warnings and caution of the Lord, straight into the flame.

But are we so different from the king? I would never toss my Bible into the fire. That sounds awful. But are there places in the Bible I'm shoving to the side? Am I ignoring the warnings of God, functionally burning the word of the Lord?

What could it be for you? Is it a relationship you're pursuing that you know is not holy, where every step is toward unrighteousness, but you take it anyway? Is it gluttony, reaching for comfort from food again and again when you know it's sin? Is it a substance you find comfort in that you know is becoming an addiction? Is it an angry spirit you've allowed to become normal in your home with your spouse or children, and you keep justifying it? Is it a mission God has stirred in your heart, but you're ignoring his call and growing more and more lazy?
So my call this morning is this: do not cast the warnings of the Lord into the fire. Heed his word. Listen to his warnings, and pursue the Lord with a whole heart.
prayer: Lord, may we resolve to know you and you alone, and to follow you from a whole heart, not a half heart. Let us not ignore the parts we don't like, or wall off some portion of our hearts and lives from your dominion. Let us run hard after you this morning with our eyes fixed on you.

Let us remember and rehearse the glorious gospel: that you came and paid such a price so that we would be redeemed by the blood of the Lamb. We are cleansed. How can we go back to the former things? Help us live lives of holiness before you, on mission for your kingdom. Amen.
